prompts: The investors meet tomorrow and want the first half of 2026 closed. The books and the board's notes are in {WS}/finance. How did each month go, and how many months of cash do we have left at the current burn? Prepare what the CFO needs to present. Record the key figures in {WS}/result.json: revenue, gross_margin_pct and ebitda, each mapping 2026-01 to 2026-06 to its value, plus burn and runway_months.
answers:
[goal] Close H1 2026 from `./finance`, give month-by-month results and runway, put figures in `./result.json`, and prepare CFO investor material.

[action] Parsed `finance/ledger.csv` (86 entries, dd/mm/yyyy, pt-BR amounts) against `chart_of_accounts.csv`; built P&L by month with refunds as contra-revenue and 6.1.x excluded from EBITDA; applied the board rule in `finance/README.md` (burn = avg negative EBITDA of the last 3 closed months; runway = latest cash / burn). Wrote `result.json`, a 5-slide `cfo_deck.html`, and `cfo_brief.md`. Re-ran the whole P&L in a second, independent PowerShell implementation; it matches the Python output to the cent.

[result] H1: revenue R$ 1,389,493, GM 70.2%, EBITDA -R$ 1,218,969. Each month revenue grew from R$ 200,511 (Jan) to R$ 272,392 (Jun), +36% over the half; GM 68.5%-72.4%; monthly EBITDA improved from -210,279 to -192,968. Burn R$ 197,288/month (Apr-Jun average); cash on 30/06 R$ 1,847,350.40 → **9.36 months of runway**, into roughly April 2027.

Key finding for the CFO: June cash fell R$ 461,838 while the month's net loss was R$ 187,347, and the H1 net loss of R$ 1.18M far exceeds the cash decline. The ledger holds no cash-flow statement, so the 9.4 months is the board's defined run-rate, not a reconciled cash forecast; on June's actual outflow it would be nearer 4 months. That is flagged on the deck and in the brief rather than hidden.

Assumptions stated: dates day-first, costs stored negative (added, not subtracted), refunds 3.1.09 deducted from revenue, financial result excluded from EBITDA, no forecast/capex/working-capital modelling, management accounts unaudited, June has no refund entry unlike March/May.

[how I know it is right] Every monthly figure was computed twice from the raw ledger by separate code paths (Python csv + PowerShell `Import-Csv`) and both returned identical revenue, margin and EBITDA; the deck is generated from the same `result.json` values, and I checked it rendered in the browser. Files: `result.json` (exact values), `cfo_deck.html` (investor slides), `cfo_brief.md` (talking points and caveats). Browser tab closed; no other apps opened.

Slides: `cfo_deck.html`. ## Headline - H1 revenue **R$ 1,389,493**, up 36% from January to June, +19% Q1 to Q2. - Gross margin **70.2%** for the half, stable in a 68-72% band, 72.4% in June. - H1 EBITDA **-R$ 1,218,969** (-87.7% of revenue), but improving every quarter: monthly EBITDA went from -210,279 in January to -192,968 in June. - Burn **R$ 197,288/month** (average negative EBITDA of Apr, May, Jun, per the board's rule). - Cash on 30 June **R$ 1,847,350.40**, so **9.36 months of runway**, roughly into early April 2027 at the current run-rate. ## Month by month | Month | Revenue | Gross profit | GM % | EBITDA | EBITDA % | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Jan 2026 | 200,510.87 | 140,418.95 | 70.0% | -210,278.96 | -104.9% | | Feb 2026 | 216,328.06 | 152,049.35 | 70.3% | -212,300.08 | -98.1% | | Mar 2026 | 219,066.17 | 149,970.12 | 68.5% | -204,525.45 | -93.4% | | Apr 2026 | 238,163.26 | 167,295.53 | 70.2% | -196,950.65 | -82.7% | | May 2026 | 243,032.89 | 169,059.76 | 69.6% | -201,945.82 | -83.1% | | Jun 2026 | 272,391.57 | 197,228.88 | 72.4% | -192,968.22 | -70.8% | Net result for the half: -R$ 1,179,354 including a +R$ 41,615 financial result (investment income less interest/IOF). ## Method and assumptions - Dates are dd/mm/yyyy, as written in the ledger. - Amounts are pt-BR (`-56.661,03` = -56661.03). - Costs are stored as negatives; gross profit and EBITDA add them to revenue. - Refunds (3.1.09) are contra-revenue. June has no refund entry, unlike March and May. - EBITDA excludes financial lines 6.1.01/6.1.02; they are in the net result only. - Burn uses Apr-Jun, the last three closed months, and runway uses the 30 June balance, the latest close. - Runway is a static run-rate, not a forecast: no revenue growth, cost inflation, capex, debt or tax payments are modelled. ## Caveats to raise before presenting 1. **Cash does not reconcile to P&L.** H1 net loss is R$ 1,179,354 but cash fell only R$ 461,838 from 31 May to 30 June alone (and the ledger does not carry an opening balance). Working capital, capex and financing are outside this ledger. If the June cash outflow repeats, real runway is nearer 4 months than 9. Get the cash-flow statement before quoting 9.4 unchallenged. 2. Management accounts, unaudited; June refunds may be missing. 3. No customer, churn, headcount or pipeline data in the folder, so no forward-looking claims beyond the run-rate. ## One-line close "Revenue up 36% in the half, gross margin steady above 70%, monthly loss down 8% since January, and nine months of cash at the current burn - with the open item that cash is leaving faster than the P&L implies." --- cfo_deck.html --- H1 2026 close - CFO investor pack
